topicName: P9 States Of Matter And Changes Of State

steps.title: Density
steps.body: The mass per unit volume of a substance, measured in kg/m³. Density tells us how compact a substance is.

steps.title: Internal energy
steps.body: The total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles in a substance.

steps.title: Specific latent heat
steps.body: The amount of energy required to change the state of 1 kg of a substance without changing its temperature.

steps.title: Specific latent heat of fusion
steps.body: The energy required to change 1 kg of a substance from solid to liquid (melt) at its melting point.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Regular objects Measure the dimensions (length, width, height) using a ruler, vernier calliper or micrometer Calculate volume using the appropriate formula (e.g. V = l × w × h for a cuboid) Measure mass using a balance Calculate density: ρ = m / V Irregular objects (displacement method) Measure the mass using a balance Fill a measuring cylinder or Eureka can with water Lower the object into the water Record the volume of water displaced — this equals the volume of the object Calculate density: ρ = m / V Eureka can: A container with a spout. Fill it until water just starts to drip from the spout, then lower the object in. Collect the water that overflows — this volume equals the object's volume. Worked Example 3: Displacement method An irregular stone has a mass of 120 g. When lowered into a measuring cylinder, the water level rises from 45 cm³ to 90 cm³. Calculate the density. V = 90 − 45 = 45 cm³ ρ = m / V = 120 / 45 = 2.67 g/cm³ In kg/m³: 2.67 × 1000 = 2670 kg/m³

steps.body: Foundation Describe the arrangement and movement of particles in a gas. | Foundation A metal block has a mass of 2.7 kg and a volume of 0.001 m³.
